stated: The Conservative Party will pass a Renters Reform Bill to deliver fairness in the rental market, fully abolishing Section 21 evictions while strengthening other grounds for landlords to evict private tenants guilty of anti-social behaviour.

source.quote: We will pass a Renters Reform Bill that will deliver fairness in the rental market for landlords and renters alike. We will deliver the court reforms necessary to fully abolish Section 21 and strengthen other grounds for landlords to evict private tenants guilty of anti-social behaviour.

bearing_set.reason: Abolishing Section 21 no-fault evictions directly affects security of tenure and rental market conditions, materially impacting affordability and stability for renters.
Strengthening landlord grounds to evict tenants for anti-social behaviour directly affects safety and community security outcomes.

Removing no-fault eviction means landlords must now state and justify grounds in court, giving tenants meaningful due process rights where previously none existed; this directly advances the due-process and rule-of-law indicators under O9, including protection against retaliatory eviction for tenants who exercise legal rights.

membership_note: Two fundamentals bear clearly: O1 for the direct tenure-security improvement and the plausible supply-side affordability harm; O9 for the procedural/due-process gain tenants acquire when landlords must state and justify eviction grounds. The ASB-eviction strengthening is secondary machinery that does not independently move O5 at any non-negligible scale.
